sources.title: DSA Ultimate Index
sources.label: DSA
sources.summary: Pattern-first LeetCode prep with company tags, lists, notes, and a 14-week plan.

sections.title: Two Pointer Patterns
sections.tagline: Use two indices to traverse a structure in coordinated ways — converge, chase, or scan from both ends.
rows: When to use. Sorted arrays, palindrome checks, in-place mutation, linked-list cycle/middle detection, and any O(n²) brute force that can collapse to O(n).
Key idea. Maintain two pointers with an invariant (sum, distance, parity) and advance them based on a comparison; eliminate one direction of search per step.
Complexity. Typically O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

subsections.title: Converging
subsections.description: Pointers start at both ends and move toward the middle, eliminating impossible pairs by comparison.

subsections.title: String Reversal
subsections.description: Two pointers swap characters from both ends to reverse a string or its words in place.

subsections.title: In-place Array Modification
subsections.description: A read pointer scans; a write pointer places kept elements — classic remove/move/partition.

subsections.title: Fast and Slow
subsections.description: Slow advances by 1, fast by 2 — used for cycle detection (Floyd's), middle, and duplicates.

subsections.title: Fixed Separation
subsections.description: Two pointers separated by a fixed gap k — useful for 'nth from end' and sliding-distance problems.

subsections.title: String Comparison with Special Characters
subsections.description: Two pointers running through strings that contain backspaces (#) or wildcards — process specials lazily.

subsections.title: Expanding From Center
subsections.description: Pick each index as the center and expand outward — used for palindromic substring counting.

sections.title: Array/Matrix Manipulation Patterns
sections.tagline: Manipulate 1D arrays and 2D matrices in place — rotations, traversals, marking, and prefix transforms.
rows: When to use. When you must avoid extra O(n) space, when matrix geometry matters (rotation, spiral, diagonal), or when one pass with bookkeeping replaces multiple passes.
Key idea. Use indices, signs, or sentinel values inside the existing array as bookkeeping; transform geometry by swapping layers/rows/columns.
Complexity. O(n) or O(rows×cols) time, O(1) extra space when fully in-place.

subsections.title: In-place Rotation
subsections.description: Rotate a matrix or array in place using transpose + reverse, or layer-by-layer cyclic shifts.

subsections.title: Spiral Traversal
subsections.description: Walk a matrix in spiral order by maintaining four shrinking boundaries.

subsections.title: Set Matrix Zeroes / In-place Marking
subsections.description: Use the first row/column or a sign bit as in-place markers to mark zero rows/columns without extra space.

subsections.title: Product Except Self / Prefix-Suffix Products
subsections.description: Compute prefix products from the left and suffix products from the right, then combine — avoids division.

subsections.title: Plus One / Handling Carry
subsections.description: Treat the array as a big integer; propagate carry from the least-significant digit.

subsections.title: Merge Sorted Array / In-place from End
subsections.description: Merge two sorted arrays in place starting from the largest element and writing backward.

subsections.title: Cyclic Sort
subsections.description: Place each value at index value-1 by swapping — finds missing/duplicate numbers in O(n) O(1).

subsections.title: Matrix Search / Sorted Matrix
subsections.description: Binary-search a row-and-column-sorted matrix by treating it as 1D, or staircase-search from a corner.

subsections.title: Prefix Sum / Running Sum
subsections.description: Maintain a running cumulative sum to answer subarray-sum or count-prefix-target queries.

subsections.title: Kadane Variant for Maximum Product
subsections.description: Track both the running max product and running min product (sign flips matter).

sections.title: Linked List Manipulation Patterns
sections.tagline: Surgical pointer manipulation on singly/doubly linked lists — reverse, merge, partition, and detect.
rows: When to use. Whenever the input is a linked list and you need O(1) extra space, or when the problem implies in-place restructuring.
Key idea. Use a dummy head node and 2–3 pointers (prev, curr, next) to rewire links without losing references.
Complexity. O(n) time, O(1) extra space for most variants.

subsections.title: In-place Reversal
subsections.description: Iteratively reverse links with prev/curr/next pointers; recursive variant also classic.

subsections.title: Merging Two Sorted Lists
subsections.description: Use a dummy head + tail pointer; advance the smaller front each step.

subsections.title: Addition of Numbers
subsections.description: Add digit-by-digit with a carry, advancing both list pointers.

subsections.title: Intersection Detection
subsections.description: Align two lists by length difference, then advance together until they meet (or use cycle-style trick).

subsections.title: Reordering / Partitioning
subsections.description: Split the list around a pivot (value, midpoint) and reattach — partition or zigzag-reorder.

sections.title: Tree Traversal Patterns (DFS & BFS)
sections.tagline: Recursive and iterative tree traversals — BFS for level-by-level, DFS preorder/inorder/postorder for structure.
rows: When to use. Binary trees, BSTs, n-ary trees, level-order problems, ancestor problems, path/sum problems, and serialization.
Key idea. Pick the traversal that exposes the property you need — inorder for sorted BST, postorder for child-then-self computation, BFS for shortest depth.
Complexity. O(n) time, O(h) space (h = height) for recursion stack, O(width) for BFS.

subsections.title: Tree BFS - Level Order Traversal
subsections.description: BFS with a queue; process the entire current level before moving on — level lists, right view, zigzag.

subsections.title: Tree DFS - Recursive Preorder Traversal
subsections.description: Visit root, then left subtree, then right — used for tree cloning, serialization, path building.

subsections.title: Tree DFS - Recursive Inorder Traversal
subsections.description: Visit left, root, right — yields sorted order on a BST; used for kth-smallest, BST validation.

subsections.title: Tree DFS - Recursive Postorder Traversal
subsections.description: Visit left, right, then root — used when children's results are needed before computing the parent.

subsections.title: Tree - Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) Finding
subsections.description: Find the deepest node that has both target nodes in its subtree — recursive or with parent pointers.

subsections.title: Tree - Serialization and Deserialization
subsections.description: Encode a tree to a string (preorder with nulls) and decode it back; used for cloning across the wire.

sections.title: Sliding Window Patterns
sections.tagline: Maintain a window over a sequence that grows/shrinks based on a condition — fixed-size or variable.
rows: When to use. Contiguous subarrays/substrings with sum, length, distinct-count, or frequency constraints.
Key idea. Two pointers define the window; expand the right, contract the left when the condition is violated, track answer on each valid window.
Complexity. O(n) amortized — each element enters and exits the window once.

subsections.title: Fixed Size / Subarray Calculation
subsections.description: Window of constant size k — slide one step at a time, update the aggregate in O(1).

subsections.title: Variable Size / Condition-Based
subsections.description: Grow the right pointer; shrink the left while a constraint is violated — captures max/min subarray meeting a condition.

subsections.title: Monotonic Queue for Max/Min
subsections.description: A deque of indices keeps candidates in monotonic order — answers 'max in window' in O(n).

subsections.title: Character Frequency Matching
subsections.description: Maintain a frequency map and a 'match count' — used for anagram windows and permutation-in-string.

sections.title: Stack Patterns
sections.tagline: LIFO data structure for matching, expression evaluation, and monotonic-property problems.
rows: When to use. Balanced brackets, next-greater/next-smaller, expression parsing, simulation with backtracking, histogram problems.
Key idea. Push when a condition is open or unresolved; pop when it's matched/closed. A monotonic stack maintains sorted order to answer range queries.
Complexity. O(n) amortized; each element pushed/popped at most once.

subsections.title: Valid Parentheses Matching
subsections.description: Push openers, pop on matching closer — extends to multi-bracket and nested expressions.

subsections.title: Monotonic Stack
subsections.description: Stack maintained in increasing or decreasing order — pops give next-greater/smaller in O(n).

subsections.title: Expression Evaluation / RPN / Infix
subsections.description: Two stacks for operators and operands, or evaluate Reverse Polish Notation directly.

subsections.title: Simulation / Backtracking Helper
subsections.description: Use a stack to mimic recursion or to roll back state — DFS without recursion, undo-redo.

subsections.title: Min Stack Design
subsections.description: Auxiliary stack tracks the running minimum — getMin() in O(1).

subsections.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
subsections.description: Monotonic stack of bar indices; on pop, compute the rectangle bounded by current and the new top.

sections.title: Heap (Priority Queue) Patterns
sections.tagline: Priority queue for streaming top-K, median, k-way merge, and scheduling problems.
rows: When to use. When you need the smallest/largest k elements, repeatedly extract min/max, or schedule by cost/deadline/frequency.
Key idea. Maintain a heap of size k (for top-k) or two heaps balanced around the median; push/pop are O(log n).
Complexity. O(n log k) for top-k, O(log n) per insert/extract.

subsections.title: Top K Elements / Selection / Frequency
subsections.description: Min-heap of size k to find the k largest, or max-heap of size k for k smallest.

subsections.title: Two Heaps for Median Finding
subsections.description: Max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half — top of either gives the median.

subsections.title: K-way Merge
subsections.description: Heap of (value, list_id) entries pulls the smallest across k sorted lists.

subsections.title: Scheduling / Minimum Cost with Priority Queue
subsections.description: Heap selects the highest-cost/highest-priority task at each step — task scheduling, IPO, sticks.

sections.title: Binary Search Patterns
sections.tagline: Logarithmic search on a monotonic structure — sorted arrays, rotated arrays, or 'monotonic predicate on the answer'.
rows: When to use. Sorted/rotated input, or when you can frame the answer as 'find the smallest/largest value for which a check function flips from false to true.'
Key idea. Maintain [lo, hi] with an invariant; halve the range each step. The hardest variant is binary search on the answer (parametric search).
Complexity. O(log n) for direct search, O(n log answer-range) for binary search on the answer.

subsections.title: On Sorted Array/List
subsections.description: Plain lower/upper bound on a sorted array — get the boilerplate right (lo<hi vs lo<=hi).

subsections.title: Find Min/Max in Rotated Sorted Array
subsections.description: Compare mid to lo/hi to identify which side is sorted; recurse into the sorted side or the other.

subsections.title: On Answer / Condition Function
subsections.description: Binary-search the answer; write a monotonic check(x) function that returns True for x≥answer.

subsections.title: Find First/Last Occurrence
subsections.description: Two-pass or single-pass lower/upper bound to find the first or last occurrence of a target.

subsections.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
subsections.description: Partition-based binary search across two arrays to find the kth-smallest in O(log min(m,n)).

sections.title: Graph Traversal Patterns (DFS & BFS)
sections.tagline: Graph traversal foundations — DFS/BFS for components, cycles, topological order, shortest paths, and connectivity.
rows: When to use. Any problem framed on nodes and edges: islands, courses, network flow, dependencies, coloring, MST.
Key idea. Choose the right traversal: DFS for path/cycle/topological, BFS for unweighted shortest path, Dijkstra for weighted, Union-Find for connectivity queries.
Complexity. O(V+E) for DFS/BFS, O((V+E) log V) for Dijkstra, O(E α(V)) for Union-Find.

subsections.title: Graph DFS - Connected Components / Island Counting
subsections.description: DFS from each unvisited cell/node to count connected components or islands.

subsections.title: Graph BFS - Connected Components / Island Counting
subsections.description: BFS variant of the above — preferred when you also need shortest path or you want to avoid recursion depth.

subsections.title: Graph DFS - Cycle Detection (Directed Graph)
subsections.description: DFS with three colors (white/gray/black) detects back edges in directed graphs.

subsections.title: Graph BFS - Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)
subsections.description: Maintain in-degrees; repeatedly take a zero-in-degree node and decrement neighbors — Kahn's algorithm.

subsections.title: Graph - Deep Copy / Cloning
subsections.description: DFS/BFS with a hashmap mapping old node → new node — copy nodes and links once each.

subsections.title: Graph - Shortest Path (Dijkstra's Algorithm)
subsections.description: Priority-queue based shortest path on non-negative weighted graphs.

subsections.title: Graph - Shortest Path (Bellman-Ford / BFS + K)
subsections.description: Bellman-Ford handles negative weights / detects negative cycles; BFS+K bounds path length.

subsections.title: Graph - Union-Find / Disjoint Set Union (DSU)
subsections.description: DSU with path compression and union by rank — near-O(1) amortized.

subsections.title: Graph - Bipartite Coloring
subsections.description: BFS/DFS coloring with two colors — fails if any edge connects same-color nodes.

subsections.title: Graph - Minimum Spanning Tree
subsections.description: Kruskal (sort edges + Union-Find) or Prim (heap-based expansion) for minimum spanning tree.

subsections.title: Graph - BFS on State Space
subsections.description: BFS where states are not graph nodes but encoded situations — word transformations, lock combinations.

sections.title: Greedy Patterns
sections.tagline: Make the locally optimal choice and prove it leads to a global optimum — often after sorting.
rows: When to use. Interval scheduling, jump-reachability, partition-labels, frequency-based scheduling, exchange-argument problems.
Key idea. Sort by the right key (start, end, deadline, ratio) and process greedily; sometimes use a heap to track 'best available' option.
Complexity. Typically O(n log n) for the sort, then O(n) for the sweep.

subsections.title: Interval Merging / Scheduling
subsections.description: Sort intervals by start (or end); merge or schedule with a single sweep.

subsections.title: Jump Game Reachability / Minimization
subsections.description: Track the farthest reachable index; greedy jump count via 'current end vs farthest seen'.

subsections.title: Buy/Sell Stock
subsections.description: Track running min cost (or running min price) and update max profit greedily.

subsections.title: Gas Station Circuit
subsections.description: Either everyone can be reached from one station, or no one can — single pass with running tank.

subsections.title: Task Scheduling / Frequency Based
subsections.description: Always schedule the most-frequent task next, separated by cooldown — heap or count-based.

subsections.title: Partition / Labels
subsections.description: Greedy partition by extending the current segment to cover the latest seen index of any character.

subsections.title: Assign / Resource Allocation
subsections.description: Sort by a property (deadline, ratio, capacity) and assign one-by-one — assignment problems, two-city scheduling.

sections.title: Backtracking Patterns
sections.tagline: Systematic exploration of decision trees — choose, recurse, un-choose — with pruning.
rows: When to use. Subsets, permutations, combinations, palindrome partitions, constraint satisfaction (N-Queens, Sudoku), path search in grids.
Key idea. Maintain a partial solution; at each step, try each valid choice, recurse, then undo. Prune branches that can't lead to a valid answer.
Complexity. Exponential in the worst case — O(2ⁿ), O(n!), or similar; pruning is critical.

subsections.title: Subsets / Include-Exclude
subsections.description: At each index, choose to include or skip — generates the 2ⁿ subsets.

subsections.title: Permutations
subsections.description: Swap each index with subsequent indices to generate all n! orderings.

subsections.title: Combination Sum
subsections.description: Recurse with remaining target; allow/disallow reuse of the same element depending on the variant.

subsections.title: Parentheses Generation
subsections.description: Track open/close counts and only emit valid prefixes (open ≥ close, both ≤ n).

subsections.title: Word Search / Path Finding in Grid
subsections.description: DFS from each cell with marked-visited and unmark-on-return — used for word search in grids.

subsections.title: N-Queens / Constraint Satisfaction
subsections.description: Place pieces one by one with conflict pruning — N-Queens, Sudoku.

subsections.title: Palindrome Partitioning
subsections.description: At each prefix, try every cut where the prefix is a palindrome; recurse on the suffix.

sections.title: Dynamic Programming (DP) Patterns
sections.tagline: Memoize overlapping subproblems and build optimal solutions from smaller ones.
rows: When to use. Optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems: knapsack, edit distance, longest common subsequence, paths in a grid, palindrome problems.
Key idea. Define state precisely, write a recurrence, decide top-down (memoization) or bottom-up (tabulation), then optimize space when possible.
Complexity. Polynomial — states × transitions; classic DPs are O(n²) or O(n·m).

subsections.title: 1D Array / Fibonacci Style
subsections.description: dp[i] depends on dp[i-1] (and maybe dp[i-2]) — climb stairs, house robber.

subsections.title: 1D Array / Kadane's Algorithm for Max/Min Subarray
subsections.description: Maintain running max-ending-here and global max — classic max-subarray.

subsections.title: 1D Array / Coin Change / Unbounded Knapsack Style
subsections.description: Unbounded knapsack — outer over items, inner over capacities in increasing order.

subsections.title: 1D Array / 0-1 Knapsack Subset Sum Style
subsections.description: 0/1 knapsack — outer over items, inner over capacities in DECREASING order to avoid reuse.

subsections.title: 1D Array / Word Break Style
subsections.description: dp[i] = OR over all dict words w of dp[i-len(w)] when s[i-len(w):i]==w.

subsections.title: 2D Array / Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
subsections.description: dp[i][j] = LCS length of prefixes; +1 on match, max otherwise.

subsections.title: 2D Array / Edit Distance
subsections.description: dp[i][j] = min ops to convert s[:i] to t[:j] via insert/delete/replace.

subsections.title: 2D Array / Unique Paths on Grid
subsections.description: dp[i][j] = ways/min-cost to reach (i,j) — usually dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1] with obstacles.

subsections.title: Interval DP
subsections.description: dp[i][j] = answer on the subarray a[i..j], iterated by increasing interval length.

subsections.title: Catalan Numbers
subsections.description: Sum dp[k]·dp[n-1-k] for k = 0..n-1 — counts binary trees, parenthesizations, polygon triangulations.

subsections.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
subsections.description: dp[i] = length of LIS ending at i; O(n²) basic, O(n log n) with patience-sort/binary search.

subsections.title: Palindrome DP
subsections.description: dp[i][j] = whether s[i..j] is a palindrome / length of longest palindromic subsequence.

sections.title: String Manipulation Patterns
sections.tagline: Character-level algorithms — palindromes, anagrams, parsing, and pattern matching.
rows: When to use. String comparison, frequency counting, integer/string conversion, substring search with linear-time guarantees.
Key idea. Use frequency arrays for anagrams, two pointers for palindromes, hashing for fast comparison, and KMP/Rabin-Karp for substring search.
Complexity. O(n) for most one-pass problems, O(n+m) for KMP, O(n) average for Rabin-Karp.

subsections.title: Palindrome Check / Two Pointers / Reverse
subsections.description: Two-pointer or reverse-and-compare to check palindromes; consider ignoring non-alphanumeric.

subsections.title: Anagram Check / Frequency Count / Sort
subsections.description: Sort characters or use frequency arrays of length 26 to compare strings as multisets.

subsections.title: Roman to Integer Conversion
subsections.description: Walk left-to-right; subtract when a smaller numeral precedes a larger one.

subsections.title: String to Integer (atoi)
subsections.description: Skip whitespace, capture sign, parse digits with overflow clamping.

subsections.title: Multiply Strings / Manual Simulation
subsections.description: Simulate grade-school multiplication digit-by-digit into an int array.

subsections.title: String Matching / Naive / KMP / Rabin-Karp
subsections.description: Naive O(nm) substring search; KMP and Rabin-Karp give O(n+m) and O(n) average.

subsections.title: Repeated Substring Pattern Detection
subsections.description: Use KMP failure function or string concatenation tricks to detect periodic patterns.

sections.title: Bit Manipulation Patterns
sections.tagline: Use binary representation as a data structure — XOR for cancellation, AND/OR for masks, shifts for power-of-two.
rows: When to use. Finding singletons in pairs, counting set bits, subset enumeration via bitmask, modular arithmetic with bits.
Key idea. XOR is its own inverse (a^a=0), AND with (n-1) clears the lowest set bit, shifts multiply/divide by 2.
Complexity. Most operations are O(1) per bit, O(log n) per number.

subsections.title: Bitwise XOR / Finding Single or Missing Number
subsections.description: XOR all elements — pairs cancel, leaving the singleton.

subsections.title: Bitwise AND / Counting Set Bits
subsections.description: Count set bits with n & (n-1) until n is zero.

subsections.title: Bitwise DP / Counting Bits Optimization
subsections.description: dp[i] = dp[i>>1] + (i&1) — counts set bits for 0..n.

subsections.title: Bitwise Operations / Power of Two or Four Check
subsections.description: n & (n-1) == 0 ⇔ power of two; mask with 0x55555555 for power of four.

sections.title: Design Patterns
sections.tagline: Build data structures with the right operation guarantees — O(1) cache, O(log n) ordered set, Trie prefix lookup.
rows: When to use. Interview prompts that start with 'Design a class that supports …' — LRU, LFU, Twitter feed, hit counter, autocomplete.
Key idea. Compose primitives — hashmap + doubly linked list for LRU, hashmap + heap for top-K, Trie for prefix queries.
Complexity. Operation-specific — the goal is usually O(1) or O(log n) per call.

subsections.title: General / Specific Data Structure Design
subsections.description: Compose hashmap + secondary structure (linked list, heap, set) to give each operation the right complexity.

subsections.title: Trie / Prefix Tree Design
subsections.description: Insert/search words in O(L); add wildcard matching for advanced variants.

sections.title: Segment Tree & Fenwick Tree Patterns
sections.tagline: Tree-based range data structures — segment tree for arbitrary range queries, Fenwick (BIT) for prefix sums.
rows: When to use. Range sum/min/max with point or range updates, inversion counting, online interval problems, coordinate compression.
Key idea. Segment tree is more flexible (lazy propagation for range updates); Fenwick is simpler and faster for prefix-sum style queries.
Complexity. O(n) build, O(log n) per query/update.

subsections.title: Segment Tree / Range Query with Updates
subsections.description: Build a binary tree of intervals; each internal node stores an aggregate (sum/min/max). Lazy propagation handles range updates.

subsections.title: Fenwick Tree / Binary Indexed Tree / Coordinate Compression
subsections.description: BIT supports point update + prefix sum in O(log n); coordinate-compress when indices are sparse.

sections.title: Prefix Sum & Difference Array Patterns
sections.tagline: Precompute cumulative sums for O(1) range queries; combine with hashmap for 'subarray equals target' even with negatives.
rows: When to use. Subarray sum problems where sliding window fails (e.g., when negatives are allowed), range sum queries, range updates via difference array.
Key idea. prefix[i] = a[0]+…+a[i-1]; range sum = prefix[r+1]-prefix[l]. With hashmap, count subarrays whose prefix difference equals k.
Complexity. O(n) build, O(1) per range query; difference array gives O(1) range updates.

subsections.title: Subarray Sum with Hashmap
subsections.description: Hashmap of running prefix sums → count subarrays whose sum equals k, even with negatives.

subsections.title: Range Sum Query (Static)
subsections.description: Precompute prefix array once; answer range sums in O(1) (1D and 2D variants).

subsections.title: Difference Array / Range Update
subsections.description: diff[l] += v, diff[r+1] -= v on range updates; prefix-sum the diff array at the end.

subsections.title: Prefix XOR / Prefix Product
subsections.description: Prefix XOR or prefix product to answer range-XOR / range-product queries.

sections.title: Hash Map & Cache Design Patterns
sections.tagline: Hash structures + auxiliary lists for O(1) lookup, insertion, and eviction.
rows: When to use. Frequency grouping, consecutive-sequence detection, and cache designs (LRU/LFU/time-based/random-O(1)).
Key idea. Compose a hashmap with a doubly linked list (LRU), or hashmap+frequency map+ordered keys (LFU). The map gives O(1) lookup; the list gives O(1) reorder.
Complexity. O(1) per operation for well-designed caches.

subsections.title: Grouping / Frequency
subsections.description: Hashmap groups elements by a canonical key (sorted string, character signature, etc.).

subsections.title: LRU Cache Design
subsections.description: Doubly linked list orders by recency; hashmap maps key → list node for O(1) access.

subsections.title: LFU Cache Design
subsections.description: Two hashmaps: one for value, one for the frequency-bucket list head; promote on access.

subsections.title: Time-Based / Snapshot Storage
subsections.description: Hashmap of stacks (or arrays) keyed by snapshot id / version / timestamp for time-travel queries.

subsections.title: Hashmap + Random Access O(1)
subsections.description: Hashmap maps value → index; backing array supports O(1) random pick via swap-and-pop.

sections.title: Math, Number Theory & Geometry Patterns
sections.tagline: Number theory, modular arithmetic, geometry, and combinatorics — the math underneath many interview problems.
rows: When to use. GCD/LCM, primes, modular exponentiation, integer/string number conversion, point/line/rectangle geometry, k-nearest points.
Key idea. Know the closed-form identities (Euclid's GCD, sieve of Eratosthenes, fast power) and the geometric primitives (cross product, distance squared).
Complexity. O(log n) for GCD/fast-power, O(n log log n) for sieve, O(n) for most geometry sweeps.

subsections.title: Powers, Logs, Roots
subsections.description: Closed-form / iterative number theory — fast power, GCD, sieve, modular inverse.

subsections.title: Number Representation Conversion
subsections.description: Convert integers to/from Roman numerals, English words, Excel column titles.

subsections.title: Primes & Sieve
subsections.description: Sieve of Eratosthenes / linear sieve for prime queries; trial division for one-off checks.

subsections.title: Geometry & Points
subsections.description: Cross product, dot product, distance², bounding rectangles, lattice/grid geometry.

subsections.title: GCD, LCM & Combinatorics
subsections.description: Combinations C(n,k), Pascal triangle, modular nCr with Fermat's little theorem.

sections.title: Trie / Prefix Tree Patterns
sections.tagline: A 26-ary (or 2-ary for XOR) tree where each path from root spells a string prefix.
rows: When to use. Prefix lookup, autocomplete, word search in grids, replace-words, palindrome pairs, maximum-XOR-pair queries.
Key idea. Insert/search are O(L) where L is word length; combine with DFS/backtracking when searching a grid for many words at once.
Complexity. O(sum of word lengths) to build, O(L) per query.

subsections.title: Trie Core (Insert/Search)
subsections.description: Children dict/array + isEnd flag; insert and search in O(L).

subsections.title: Trie with Wildcards
subsections.description: Extend search to handle '.' or '*' wildcards via DFS branching.

subsections.title: Trie + DFS on Grid / Strings
subsections.description: Build a Trie of words; DFS the grid and walk the Trie in parallel.

subsections.title: Streaming / Autocomplete / Suffix Trie
subsections.description: Insert/remove on demand and answer streaming queries (suffix matching, autocomplete).

subsections.title: XOR Trie / Binary Trie
subsections.description: Binary Trie where each node has children 0/1; query the bit-by-bit complement to maximize XOR.

sections.title: Intervals & Line Sweep Patterns
sections.tagline: Sort intervals or convert them to point events; sweep a line across the timeline.
rows: When to use. Merging intervals, meeting-rooms concurrency, calendar booking, skyline silhouettes, range-coloring.
Key idea. Sort by start (and sometimes by end); for line sweep, emit +1/−1 events at endpoints and sweep to find max concurrent count.
Complexity. O(n log n) for the sort/sweep.

subsections.title: Interval Merging / Insertion
subsections.description: Sort by start; merge/insert into a result list when they overlap.

subsections.title: Meeting Rooms & Scheduling
subsections.description: Sort and compare current's end with the previous — counts overlaps or schedules.

subsections.title: Line Sweep with Events
subsections.description: Convert intervals to +1/−1 point events on a sorted timeline; sweep to compute peaks.

subsections.title: Calendar / Booking (TreeMap)
subsections.description: Use a TreeMap of bookings, or two-pass overlap counting, to handle dynamic add/query.

sections.title: Tree Dynamic Programming Patterns
sections.tagline: Post-order DP on trees — each subtree returns one or more values used by its parent.
rows: When to use. House Robber on a tree, diameter, max path sum, longest univalue path, max-sum BST.
Key idea. Recurse to children first; combine their return values (often a tuple like (include, exclude) or (max_path_ending_here, best_seen)) to compute the parent's answer.
Complexity. O(n) — each node is visited once.

subsections.title: Include/Exclude on Tree (Tree Robber)
subsections.description: Each node returns (include_me, exclude_me); parent picks max — works for House Robber on tree.

subsections.title: Tree Diameter & Longest Path
subsections.description: Each node returns max-depth-going-down; while recursing, update the global diameter answer.

subsections.title: Tree Max Path Sum / Tilt
subsections.description: Each node returns max-gain-as-leaf; while recursing, update the global max-path-sum answer.

subsections.title: Subtree Summary DP
subsections.description: Each node returns subtree summary (size, sum, valid?) — used for largest valid BST in a tree.

sections.title: Advanced Dynamic Programming Patterns
sections.tagline: DP where state encodes a subset (bitmask), a digit position (digit DP), or a finite mode (state machine).
rows: When to use. Small-n exponential problems (n ≤ 20 for bitmask), counting integers ≤ N with digit constraints, stock problems with cooldown/fee.

Key idea. Bitmask DP: state = (mask, …); iterate over submasks or transitions. Digit DP: state = (position, tight, leading_zero, …). State machine: track which 'mode' you're in (holding, sold, cooldown).
Complexity. Bitmask: O(2ⁿ · n). Digit: O(digits · states · 10). State machine: O(n · states).

subsections.title: Bitmask / Subset DP / TSP-style
subsections.description: dp[mask] over subsets of n elements (n ≤ 20); iterate over submasks for partition/TSP problems.

subsections.title: Digit DP
subsections.description: Digit DP — state (pos, tight, leading_zero, last_digit) counts integers with digit constraints up to N.

subsections.title: State-Machine DP (Stock & Beyond)
subsections.description: State machine — track 'holding/sold/cooldown' or finite mode transitions for stock/path problems.

subsections.title: Interval / Partition DP
subsections.description: Interval/partition DP — dp[i][j] from splits k between i and j; #312 Burst Balloons is canonical.

subsections.title: Grid-Cost DP (Paint House / Cherry Pickup)
subsections.description: Cost-on-grid DP with constraints (paint house, cherry pickup, dungeon, falling path).

sections.title: Advanced Graph Algorithm Patterns
sections.tagline: Algorithms beyond basic BFS/DFS — bridges, all-pairs, Eulerian paths, A*-style heuristics, 0-1 BFS.
rows: When to use. Critical edges, all-pairs shortest path on small graphs, itinerary reconstruction, weighted-grid shortest paths, multi-state BFS.
Key idea. Tarjan for bridges/SCC, Floyd-Warshall for all-pairs (O(V³)), Hierholzer for Eulerian, 0-1 BFS for graphs with edge weights ∈ {0,1}, bidirectional BFS to halve depth.
Complexity. Tarjan O(V+E), Floyd-Warshall O(V³), Bellman-Ford O(V·E), 0-1 BFS O(V+E).

subsections.title: Tarjan: Bridges, Articulation, SCC
subsections.description: Tarjan's DFS with discovery/low-link arrays identifies bridges (critical connections) and SCCs.

subsections.title: Eulerian Path (Hierholzer)
subsections.description: Hierholzer's algorithm — DFS with edge-removal builds the Eulerian path/circuit.

subsections.title: All-Pairs Shortest Path (Floyd-Warshall)
subsections.description: Floyd-Warshall — O(V³) DP over intermediate vertices computes all-pairs shortest paths.

subsections.title: Bellman-Ford / BFS with K Steps
subsections.description: Bellman-Ford handles negatives; with K-step limit (BFS+K), bounds path length for cheapest-flights.

subsections.title: Dijkstra Variants on Weighted Grids
subsections.description: Dijkstra on weighted grids: distance metric is max-edge-on-path, min-effort, or probability product.

subsections.title: 0-1 BFS (Deque Variant)
subsections.description: 0-1 BFS uses a deque: push-front on weight-0 edges, push-back on weight-1; O(V+E).

subsections.title: Bidirectional BFS / State-Space BFS
subsections.description: Bidirectional BFS from start AND end — halves search radius, used for word ladder.

subsections.title: Topological-Sort Applications
subsections.description: Topological-sort applications: scheduling, alien dictionary, sequence reconstruction, course graphs.

subsections.title: Functional Graph / Safe-State Analysis
subsections.description: Functional graph / safe-state analysis: detect nodes whose out-paths all terminate in a sink.

sections.title: Multi-Source BFS Patterns
sections.tagline: Seed the BFS queue with ALL starting cells at distance 0 and expand simultaneously.
rows: When to use. Multi-origin shortest-distance problems on grids: rotting fruit, walls and gates, distance to nearest 1, fire spread.
Key idea. Push every source into the queue with distance 0 in the same pass; the BFS naturally computes the minimum distance from any source.
Complexity. O(rows × cols) — every cell is visited once.

subsections.title: Multi-Source Distance BFS
subsections.description: Seed all source cells with distance 0 in the same pass; BFS expands all fronts together.

sections.title: Iterator & Data-Stream Design Patterns
sections.tagline: Lazy iteration over nested/structured data, plus streaming statistics on infinite input.
rows: When to use. BST iterator, peeking iterator, zigzag iterator, nested list flattening, moving averages, streaming median.
Key idea. Defer work until next() is called; keep just enough state (stack of partial results, two heaps, deque) to answer the next query in O(1) or O(log n).
Complexity. Typically O(1) amortized per next()/hasNext().

subsections.title: BST Iterator
subsections.description: BST iterator with controlled stack to give in-order next() in amortized O(1).

subsections.title: Peeking / Wrapping Iterators
subsections.description: Wrap an existing iterator with peek() by buffering one element.

subsections.title: Multi-Source Iterators
subsections.description: Multi-list iterators that round-robin or zigzag across sub-iterators.

subsections.title: Nested List / 2D Iterator
subsections.description: Flatten nested integers/lists with a stack of iterators or recursive expansion on demand.

subsections.title: Streaming Statistics
subsections.description: Streaming statistics — moving average via deque, median via two heaps.

subsections.title: Stack / Queue Conversion
subsections.description: Stack-of-queues / queue-of-stacks design to mimic the opposite ADT.

sections.title: Sorting Algorithms & Selection Patterns
sections.tagline: Use a sort (or partial sort) as the core technique — Quickselect, merge-sort applications, bucket/counting/radix sort.
rows: When to use. Kth-element queries (Quickselect O(n) avg), inversion counting (merge sort), bounded-range counting (bucket/radix).
Key idea. Quickselect partitions around a pivot like Quicksort but recurses into one side; merge sort can count inversions during the merge step.
Complexity. Quickselect O(n) avg / O(n²) worst; merge-sort apps O(n log n); bucket/radix O(n + k).

subsections.title: Quickselect (Kth element)
subsections.description: Partition around a pivot like Quicksort, but recurse only into the side containing the kth index.

subsections.title: Merge-Sort Applications
subsections.description: Merge sort with an extra counter increments when merging — counts inversions in O(n log n).

subsections.title: Bucket / Counting / Radix Sort
subsections.description: Place items into buckets keyed by value/frequency; concatenate the buckets in order.

subsections.title: Custom-Comparator Sort
subsections.description: Sort with a non-default comparator that captures the required ordering (e.g., 'a+b' vs 'b+a').

sections.title: Randomized Algorithm Patterns
sections.tagline: Uniform/weighted random selection in constant space, or sampling from streams of unknown length.
rows: When to use. Pick random element from a stream/linked list, weighted random by frequency, random with blacklist, Fisher–Yates shuffle.
Key idea. Reservoir sampling keeps one or k samples and replaces with probability k/i at step i; weighted random uses prefix sums + binary search.
Complexity. O(n) one-pass for reservoir; O(log n) per query for weighted (after O(n) precomputation).

subsections.title: Reservoir Sampling
subsections.description: Reservoir sampling — keep one (or k) sample(s) and replace with probability k/i at step i.

subsections.title: Weighted Random (Prefix Sum + Binary Search)
subsections.description: Weighted random pick — build prefix sums of weights, then binary search a uniform random in [0, total).

subsections.title: Fisher-Yates Shuffle
subsections.description: Fisher-Yates shuffle — swap each index with a random later index for a uniform permutation.

subsections.title: Random Pick with Blacklist
subsections.description: Random pick with blacklist — map blacklisted ids in [0,k) to whitelisted ids in [k,n).

sections.title: Advanced String Algorithm Patterns
sections.tagline: Linear-time string matching and palindrome structure beyond KMP/Rabin-Karp.
rows: When to use. Longest palindromic substring in O(n) (Manacher), shortest palindrome by prefix extension (KMP failure function), repeated/duplicate substrings (rolling hash, Z-algorithm).
Key idea. Manacher reuses palindrome symmetry to avoid recomputing; Z-algorithm computes longest common prefix with every suffix; suffix automaton/array enables substring queries.
Complexity. O(n) for Manacher and Z-algorithm; O(n log n) for suffix array.

subsections.title: Manacher's Algorithm (Linear Palindrome)
subsections.description: Manacher's algorithm — O(n) longest palindromic substring by reusing palindrome symmetry.

subsections.title: Z-Algorithm / KMP Failure-Function Applications
subsections.description: KMP / Z-algorithm — O(n) failure function and longest-common-prefix-with-suffix arrays.

subsections.title: Rolling Hash Beyond Rabin-Karp
subsections.description: Rolling hash for substring fingerprinting — find duplicate/longest repeated substrings in O(n log n).

Revisit duplicate placements intentionally; duplicated problems should teach multiple patterns.

sources.summary: Distributed systems, architecture patterns, reliability, security, and classic designs.

sections.title: System Design Interview Process & Requirements
sections.tagline: Start every design with clear requirements, scale, scope, diagrams, and interviewer alignment.
rows: When. The first 10 minutes of every system design round, before drawing boxes or naming technologies.
Key idea. A strong design answer is a structured conversation: clarify, estimate, design, validate, then discuss trade-offs.

subsections.title: Requirements & Scope
subsections.description: Functional requirements, non-functional requirements, scope control, and the HLD/LLD boundary.

subsections.title: Capacity Estimation
subsections.description: Back-of-the-envelope sizing for QPS, storage, bandwidth, peak traffic, and read/write ratio.

subsections.title: Architecture Diagrams & Communication
subsections.description: C4, UML, sequence/activity diagrams, and whiteboard layout strategy for clear interviews.

subsections.title: 5-Step Interview Framework
subsections.description: A repeatable flow for clarifying, estimating, designing, deep-diving, and closing with trade-offs.

subsections.title: Senior Engineer Signals
subsections.description: The communication habits that show ownership, trade-off thinking, and operational maturity.

subsections.title: Reference Numbers & Estimation Cheat Sheet
subsections.description: Numbers and shortcuts to make estimation fast without pretending false precision.

sections.title: Core System Design Fundamentals
sections.tagline: The vocabulary and trade-offs that every later topic builds on.
rows: When. Before choosing databases, queues, caches, or cloud services.
Key idea. Most design decisions are trade-offs among latency, throughput, consistency, availability, durability, and cost.

subsections.title: Latency, Throughput & Scalability Basics
subsections.description: Core performance terms, tail latency, vertical/horizontal scaling, and throughput trade-offs.

subsections.title: Availability, Reliability & SLAs
subsections.description: Reliability targets, downtime math, redundancy, and failover models.

subsections.title: Consistency Models
subsections.description: Strong, eventual, causal, monotonic, read-your-writes, and CRDT-based consistency.

subsections.title: CAP & PACELC Theorems
subsections.description: Partition trade-offs plus the latency-vs-consistency choice when the network is healthy.

sections.title: Networking, APIs & Traffic Management
sections.tagline: How requests enter, move through, and return from distributed systems.
rows: When. Any design with clients, APIs, load balancers, global routing, real-time updates, or public ingress.
Key idea. Good traffic design separates protocol choice, routing, load balancing, gateway policy, and overload protection.

subsections.title: HTTP, TLS & Protocol Fundamentals
subsections.description: HTTP versions, status codes, idempotency, TLS, and transport-level behavior.

subsections.title: API Styles: REST, GraphQL & gRPC
subsections.description: Choosing API contracts for public clients, internal services, streaming, and schema evolution.

subsections.title: DNS, Load Balancers & Traffic Routing
subsections.description: DNS resolution, records, GeoDNS, L4/L7 load balancing, health checks, and routing algorithms.

subsections.title: Proxies, API Gateways & Service Mesh
subsections.description: Forward/reverse proxies, API gateway responsibilities, L4/L7 differences, and sidecar/service-mesh patterns.

subsections.title: Rate Limiting Algorithms
subsections.description: Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed/sliding windows, and distributed rate limiting.

subsections.title: Real-Time Communication: Polling, SSE, WebSockets & WebRTC
subsections.description: Choosing short polling, long polling, SSE, WebSockets, or WebRTC for real-time product requirements.

sections.title: Data Storage, Databases & Distribution
sections.tagline: How systems model, store, index, replicate, partition, and move data.
rows: When. Once entities, access patterns, consistency needs, and data volume are clear.
Key idea. Start from access patterns and consistency needs; then pick storage, indexes, replication, and partitioning.

subsections.title: Storage Types: Block, Object & File
subsections.description: Choosing block, object, file, blob, archive, and ephemeral storage for the workload.

subsections.title: SQL vs NoSQL Decision Framework
subsections.description: Choosing relational, document, key-value, wide-column, graph, time-series, or search stores.

subsections.title: ACID, Transactions & Isolation
subsections.description: Atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability, isolation levels, deadlocks, and two-phase commit.

subsections.title: Indexes & Query Optimization
subsections.description: B-trees, LSM trees, covering indexes, compound indexes, and query-plan thinking.

subsections.title: Replication & Read Scaling
subsections.description: Leader/follower, multi-leader, replication lag, read replicas, and failover implications.

subsections.title: Partitioning, Sharding & Data Distribution
subsections.description: Range/hash/directory partitioning, hot shards, rebalancing, and routing queries to shards.

subsections.title: Consistent Hashing & Rebalancing
subsections.description: Hash rings, virtual nodes, remapping behavior, and when consistent hashing beats modulo hashing.

subsections.title: NoSQL Internals
subsections.description: LSM trees, SSTables, quorum reads/writes, compaction, tombstones, and high-write data stores.

sections.title: Caching & Content Delivery
sections.tagline: Reducing latency and load with cache layers from process memory to the edge.
rows: When. Read-heavy systems, global content, expensive computations, hot keys, or slow origin services.
Key idea. Every cache needs a source of truth, invalidation policy, consistency story, and failure-mode plan.

subsections.title: Cache Strategies
subsections.description: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-back, refresh-ahead, and where each belongs.

subsections.title: Cache Eviction, TTL & Invalidation
subsections.description: LRU/LFU/FIFO, TTL choices, explicit invalidation, and stale-while-revalidate patterns.

subsections.title: Cache Failure Modes & Pitfalls
subsections.description: Cache stampede, penetration, avalanche, hot keys, stale data, and memory pressure.

subsections.title: Redis & Distributed Caching
subsections.description: Redis structures, clustering, sharding, persistence, eviction, and distributed-cache design.

subsections.title: CDN Caching
subsections.description: CDN PoPs, origin shields, TTL, purges, signed URLs, and static content delivery.

subsections.title: Edge Delivery & Global Acceleration
subsections.description: Edge caching, invalidation, static vs dynamic acceleration, and token-protected edge access.

sections.title: Asynchronous Messaging & Event Streaming
sections.tagline: Decoupling systems with queues, logs, streams, delivery semantics, and event-driven flows.
rows: When. Work can happen later, spikes need buffering, or services should not call each other synchronously.
Key idea. Async design trades immediate consistency for resilience, throughput, and loose coupling.

subsections.title: Message Queues vs Event Streams
subsections.description: When to use task queues, pub/sub, append-only logs, and event streams.

subsections.title: Kafka Architecture
subsections.description: Topics, partitions, brokers, leaders, replicas, consumer groups, retention, and ordering.

subsections.title: Delivery Semantics & Reliability
subsections.description: At-most-once, at-least-once, effectively-once, idempotency, retries, and dead-letter queues.

subsections.title: Event-Driven Architecture
subsections.description: Event sourcing, CQRS, outbox pattern, choreography, and eventual consistency.

sections.title: Service Architecture Patterns
sections.tagline: How applications are decomposed into services, modules, and deployable boundaries.
rows: When. When the system grows beyond one codebase, one team, or one deployment lifecycle.
Key idea. Architecture boundaries should follow ownership, data, change rate, and failure isolation.

subsections.title: Monolith vs Microservices vs Serverless
subsections.description: Choosing deployment and ownership boundaries based on complexity, scale, and team structure.

subsections.title: Microservices Patterns
subsections.description: Service discovery, API composition, saga, outbox, sidecars, and database-per-service trade-offs.

subsections.title: Clean, Layered & Hexagonal Architecture
subsections.description: Keeping domain logic independent from frameworks, databases, transport, and infrastructure.

sections.title: Reliability, Resilience & Idempotency
sections.tagline: Designing systems that degrade gracefully instead of collapsing under failure.
rows: When. Any production design with dependencies, retries, overload, high availability, or partial failure.
Key idea. Assume every dependency fails; then bound blast radius, retry safely, and preserve core user value.

subsections.title: Circuit Breakers, Bulkheads & Timeouts
subsections.description: Preventing cascading failure with isolation, deadline propagation, and fast failure.

subsections.title: Backpressure, Throttling & Load Protection
subsections.description: Protecting systems from overload with rate limits, queues, adaptive throttling, and backpressure.

subsections.title: Graceful Degradation & Load Shedding
subsections.description: Dropping noncritical work, serving fallbacks, and preserving core flows under stress.

subsections.title: Distributed Locking, Idempotency & Safe Retries
subsections.description: Lease-based locks, fencing tokens, idempotency keys, deduplication, and retry correctness.

sections.title: Distributed Systems Coordination
sections.tagline: Coordination primitives for correctness across multiple machines.
rows: When. Leader election, consensus, distributed locks, distributed transactions, or cross-service consistency are required.
Key idea. Coordination improves correctness but costs latency, availability, and operational complexity.

subsections.title: Consensus Algorithms: Raft & Paxos
subsections.description: Replicated logs, majorities, leader terms, safety, liveness, and why consensus is expensive.

subsections.title: Leader Election, Heartbeats & Failure Detection

subsections.title: Distributed Transactions & Sagas
subsections.description: 2PC, sagas, compensation, outbox, and designing correctness across services.

sections.title: Search Systems & Discovery
sections.tagline: Indexing, ranking, autocomplete, and search-serving architecture.
rows: When. The product needs full-text search, discovery, typeahead, ranking, or geospatial lookup.
Key idea. Search is a separate read model optimized for retrieval, not a replacement for the source-of-truth database.

subsections.title: Search Indexing, Ranking & Typeahead
subsections.description: Inverted indexes, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, BM25, and autocomplete architecture.

sections.title: Observability, SLOs, Testing & Delivery
sections.tagline: Knowing the system works and shipping changes without guessing.
rows: When. After the architecture is drawn, explain how you will operate, test, deploy, and debug it.
Key idea. A design is incomplete until it has telemetry, SLOs, safe rollout, and failure-verification plans.

subsections.title: Metrics, Dashboards & Alerting
subsections.description: Prometheus-style metrics, dashboards, alert routing, saturation, traffic, errors, and latency.

subsections.title: Logging & Distributed Tracing
subsections.description: Structured logs, correlation IDs, trace spans, sampling, and debugging across service boundaries.

subsections.title: SLOs, Error Budgets & Golden Signals
subsections.description: SLI/SLO/SLA definitions, error budgets, golden signals, and tracing-driven operation.

subsections.title: Testing, Chaos & Safe Deployment
subsections.description: Load, stress, soak, chaos testing, CI/CD, canary, and blue-green deployment.

sections.title: Security, Privacy & Threat Modeling
sections.tagline: Building systems that protect users, data, APIs, and infrastructure.
rows: When. Every design: mention auth, authorization, data boundaries, abuse cases, and sensitive operations.
Key idea. Security is a set of design constraints, not a final checklist after the architecture is done.

subsections.description: STRIDE, attack surfaces, data classification, encryption boundaries, scraping, and credential-stuffing defenses.

sections.tagline: Making trade-offs visible between speed, reliability, complexity, and money.
rows: When. After the baseline design works, or when constraints include budget, egress, latency, or operational load.
Key idea. Cost is an architecture property: compute, storage, network, managed services, and scaling choices all create it.

subsections.title: Cost Estimation & Build-vs-Buy Trade-offs
subsections.description: Compute, storage, egress, autoscaling economics, managed-service trade-offs, and cost/performance choices.

Key idea. Case studies are not templates to memorize; they are exercises in applying fundamentals under constraints.

sections.title: STAR Framework & Storytelling

Key idea. Situation (10%) → Task (10%) → Action (60%) → Result (20%). Spend most time on YOUR actions, not context.

sections.title: Amazon's 16 Leadership Principles
sections.tagline: The framework Amazon uses for every interview decision.
rows: When. All Amazon interviews. Useful framework for any company too.
Key idea. Each round explicitly evaluates 2-3 LPs. Prepare a story bank that maps to all 16.

subsections.title: LP 1: Customer Obsession
subsections.description: Leaders start with the customer and work backwards. They work vigorously to earn and keep customer trust.

subsections.title: LP 2: Ownership
subsections.description: Leaders are owners. They think long term and don't sacrifice long-term value for short-term results.

subsections.title: LP 3: Invent and Simplify
subsections.description: Leaders expect innovation and invention. They simplify externally and find ways to invent.

subsections.title: LP 4: Are Right, A Lot
subsections.description: Leaders have strong judgment and good instincts. They seek diverse perspectives and disconfirm their beliefs.

subsections.title: LP 5: Learn and Be Curious
subsections.description: Leaders are never done learning. They seek to improve themselves and explore new possibilities.

subsections.title: LP 6: Hire and Develop the Best
subsections.description: Leaders raise the performance bar with every hire and promotion. They develop leaders.

subsections.title: LP 7: Insist on the Highest Standards
subsections.description: Leaders have relentlessly high standards. They continually raise the bar and drive teams to deliver high quality.

subsections.title: LP 8: Think Big
subsections.description: Thinking small is a self-fulfilling prophecy. Leaders create and communicate a bold direction.

subsections.title: LP 9: Bias for Action
subsections.description: Speed matters in business. Many decisions are reversible and don't need extensive study.

subsections.title: LP 10: Frugality
subsections.description: Accomplish more with less. Constraints breed resourcefulness, self-sufficiency, and invention.

subsections.title: LP 11: Earn Trust
subsections.description: Leaders listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. They are vocally self-critical.

subsections.title: LP 12: Dive Deep
subsections.description: Leaders operate at all levels, stay connected to the details, and audit frequently. No task is beneath them.

subsections.title: LP 13: Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit
subsections.description: Leaders challenge decisions respectfully when they disagree. Once a decision is determined, they commit wholly.

subsections.title: LP 14: Deliver Results
subsections.description: Leaders focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion.

subsections.title: LP 15: Strive to be Earth's Best Employer
subsections.description: Leaders create a safer, more productive, more diverse, and more just work environment.

subsections.title: LP 16: Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility
subsections.description: Leaders are humbly aware of their impact on the world. They think about the long-term consequences.

roadmap.title: Baseline and tooling
roadmap.focus: Git, CLI fluency, language syntax, Big-O, debugging, and test hygiene.

roadmap.title: Core coding interviews
roadmap.focus: Arrays, strings, two pointers, sliding window, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, and recursion.

roadmap.title: Advanced problem solving
roadmap.focus: Dynamic programming, heaps, binary search, tries, intervals, greedy, and graph variants.

roadmap.title: Systems foundation
roadmap.focus: HTTP, DNS, load balancers, databases, caching, queues, sharding, consistency, and reliability.

roadmap.title: Cloud and production
roadmap.focus: IAM, networking, storage, compute, serverless, observability, IaC, and deployment trade-offs.

roadmap.title: Role specialization
roadmap.focus: AI engineering, RAG, agents, evals, MLOps, or deeper backend/frontend tracks based on target roles.

roadmap.title: Behavioral and mocks
roadmap.focus: Prepare STAR stories, leadership examples, failure stories, conflict stories, and live mock interviews.

additions.why: Useful for full-stack roles and missing from the original folder as a dedicated track.
Bridges DSA/system design with real implementation work.
Interviewers increasingly ask how you ship safely, not just how you code.
Security appears in system design, cloud, and backend interviews.
A project converts the roadmap into something you can explain with ownership.

dsa.title: DSA Coverage Check
notes: Keep the 609-problem pattern index as the primary practice map.
Revisit duplicate placements intentionally; duplicated problems should teach multiple patterns.
Prioritize core patterns before advanced/niche patterns unless a target company requires them.

sd.title: System Design Coverage Check
sd.source: roadmap.sh System Design + System Design Primer + GeeksforGeeks System Design Tutorial
notes: Make trade-offs explicit: consistency, latency, cost, availability, and operability.
Use classic designs as integration practice, not memorized templates.
Add security, observability, and failure-mode reasoning to every design.

cs.title: CS Fundamentals Coverage Check
cs.source: roadmap.sh Computer Science + standard interview foundations
notes: Keep OS, networking, DB, concurrency, security, and architecture as the required core.
Add compiler/runtime and distributed-systems prerequisites as review topics.
Treat CS fundamentals as support for system design and debugging interviews.

bh.title: Behavioral Coverage Check
bh.source: STAR interview prep + leadership story coverage
notes: Prepare reusable stories that can flex across companies and question wording.
Every story should include stakes, action, measurable result, and reflection.
Keep a short answer and a deeper version for each major story.

ai.title: AI Engineering Coverage Check
ai.source: roadmap.sh AI Engineer + OpenAI Cookbook + production LLM practice
notes: Focus on building reliable AI systems with existing models before training from scratch.
Pair every RAG/agent technique with evals, observability, and failure analysis.
Track safety, cost, latency, and quality as production constraints.

cloud.title: Cloud Coverage Check
notes: Keep AWS and Azure mappings side-by-side for interview recall.
Add reliability, security, cost, and operational excellence to each service family.
Practice explaining why a managed service is chosen, not only what it is called.
